title: A language worth keeping.
summary: A wide document tests the shared masthead, reading measure, and typography.
body:
## Relationships

Give each region a purpose. Orientation, working content, supporting information, and commands should have stable edges and understandable scope.

## Hierarchy

A title names the page. Metadata explains its context. Section headings divide the argument. Controls should look like controls, and sustained prose should have a bounded reading measure.

| Object | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Masthead | Title, summary, date, author, and tags |
| Navigation | Links to other destinations |
| Optional contents | Explicit links within the document when its author adds them |
| Reading column | The argument and its evidence |

## States

Appearance is a page preference, not a replacement for semantic structure. Light and dark retain the same relationships. The menu exposes its expanded state, responds to Escape, and returns focus to its trigger.

> A shared stylesheet is a contract between markup and presentation. It is not a promise that unrelated markup will look the same.

## Boundaries

These templates borrow no institutional or personal content from the source websites. Their shell is a maintained derivative of the React reference. The original websites remain unchanged.

title: Use this template.
summary: A standalone React starter with the complete Krigsvold visual shell.
body:
## Start a project

Install the native React components and their Core foundations:

```sh
npm install @krigsvold/react@0.2.1 @krigsvold/core@2.2.5
```

## Use the reference source

The standalone reference application is in `examples/react-catalog` in the [React source repository](https://github.com/krigsvolddesign/react). Its own React components provide this homepage, the shared shell, all 50 canonical examples, and the interactive application specimens.

## Make it yours

Edit the identity and destinations in `src/shell/SourceShell.tsx`, the hero in `Masthead.tsx`, and the homepage words in `ReferencePages.tsx`. Keep the bundled image attribution when using the approved photography.

[Browse all examples](/examples/) or [inspect versioned documentation](/docs/).

title: What a shell should own
summary: A dependable frame leaves room for the work.
body:
## The frame A website shell should own the recurring relationships: the site identity, navigation, masthead, reading measures, and footer. A page supplies its subject, metadata, and content. Authors may add manual inline contents above the reading content when useful. Krigsvold does not generate a contents list or place one in a page margin. ## The reading A date and an author belong with the title. Tags describe the article. They are not loose paragraphs dropped between the masthead and the opening sentence. The main text begins below the masthead. It has enough room for a sustained thought, without stretching each line across the full screen. ## The contract React prerenders the page before it reaches the browser. The shared CSS still recognizes the same masthead, container, heading, and footer classes. That is the abstraction being tested here. ```html
…
``` The markup above illustrates the Martlet masthead; Krigsvold uses its own `page-masthead` hierarchy. Shared concepts do not require identical family markup.
